comparison: Both evaluate SEMA4A expression patterns (C1-C8, C12) and find them supported. OpenEval focuses on methodological convergence across scRNA-seq, IHC, and qPCR. Peer review emphasizes the tissue-specific role and includes immune cell upregulation findings (C9-C11, C114-C115) that OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 addresses immune cell expression (C9-C11) showing differential patterns between tissue and serum. Peer R1 incorporates these claims alongside keratinocyte expression, noting Sema4A is 'upregulated in hematopoietic cells.' Both find evidence supported.

Both evaluate IMQ model findings (C13-C21) and find them supported. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence across multiple readouts and tissue-specific mechanisms. Peer review confirms the enhanced dermatitis phenotype and notes increased gdT cells and IL-17 without raising concerns.

Both evaluate IL-23 model findings (C24-C29) and find them supported. OpenEval notes this model recapitulates IMQ findings with some differences. Peer review describes this as an 'orthogonal model' providing additional support for conclusions through an independent approach.

Both evaluate bone marrow chimera experiments (C30-C37) and find them strongly supported. OpenEval emphasizes the systematic design ruling out confounds. Peer review confirms these experiments demonstrate epithelial-specific Sema4A role in maintaining skin homeostasis.

OpenEval R6 addresses temporal/spatial characterization (C38-C44) showing developmental progression and epidermal specificity. Peer R5 encompasses these claims plus immune phenotypes (C45-C58, C117-C118), describing naive KO skin as 'The most interesting finding' resembling psoriatic non-lesions. Both find evidence supported.

OpenEval R7 evaluates localized epidermal effects (C45-C58) showing tissue-specific patterns. Peer R5 includes these claims within broader evaluation of naive KO phenotype, emphasizing potential as novel psoriasis model. Both find evidence supported and note the epidermal microenvironment role.

Both evaluate human-mouse comparisons (C59-C73) and find them supported. OpenEval emphasizes convergence across RNA-seq, qPCR, immunofluorescence, and TEWL. Peer review confirms similarities between KO mice and psoriatic non-lesions, describing findings as 'convincing.'

Both evaluate mTOR activation findings (C74-C81) and find them supported. OpenEval notes consistency across species/methods but highlights that mTORC2 activation is scarcely detectable in human samples versus mice. Peer review confirms upregulation patterns without raising this concern.

Both evaluate mTOR inhibitor experiments (C82-C97) and find them supported. OpenEval notes differential mTORC1/mTORC2 roles and lack of IL-17A effect suggesting mTOR-independent mechanisms. Peer review emphasizes rapamycin's reversal of phenotypes in both naive and IMQ conditions, describing this as bolstering conclusions.

OpenEval R11 evaluates summary conclusions (C98-C103) as supported by comprehensive experimental evidence. Peer R6 addresses overlapping claims (C99-C101) within context of human-mouse comparisons, confirming the protective role interpretation.

OpenEval R11 addresses conclusions (C102-C103) as well-supported. Peer R9 includes these claims (C102-C103) alongside mechanistic speculation (C106-C110, C123), emphasizing therapeutic implications and tissue-specific protective role. Both find core conclusions supported.

Both address mechanistic speculation (C106-C110). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the Sema4A-mTOR link is correlative rather than causal and requires rescue experiments. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing therapeutic implications and describing the tissue-specific role as having 'important implications' for targeting Sema4a pharmacologically.

OpenEval R13 evaluates manuscript summary claims (C111-C123) as largely supported but notes C123 regarding therapeutic targets is speculative. Peer R1 includes summary claims C114-C115 within broader evaluation of expression findings, finding them supported as part of the 'important new concept.'
OpenEval R13 includes C116 in summary claims rated as supported. Peer R2 addresses C116 within IMQ model evaluation, confirming the enhanced inflammation phenotype without concerns.
OpenEval R13 includes C120 in summary claims rated as supported. Peer R4 addresses C120 within bone marrow chimera evaluation, confirming the epithelial-specific regulatory role.
OpenEval R13 includes C117-C118 in summary claims rated as supported. Peer R5 addresses these within naive phenotype evaluation, describing findings as potentially yielding a novel mouse model.
OpenEval R13 includes C121 in summary claims rated as supported. Peer R7 addresses C121 within mTOR activation evaluation, confirming the upregulation pattern.
OpenEval R13 includes C122 in summary claims rated as supported. Peer R8 addresses C122 within mTOR inhibitor evaluation, confirming the reversal of cytokeratin expression.

OpenEval R13 evaluates summary including C123 (therapeutic targets) as speculative requiring validation. Peer R9 rates C123 as supported, emphasizing therapeutic implications and describing findings as having 'support for the biology described here as a mechanism with therapeutic implications.'
